$comment: Every UI-contract violation the product deliberately keeps, and why. `npm run check:ui-contract` fails on anything not listed here, on a count higher OR lower than recorded, and on any entry whose rule has no `reasons` text. This began as a shrink-only inventory of 660 violations carrying `debt` tags for the migration slices that owed the work; that debt reached zero on 2026-08-25 and the `debt` escape hatch was removed with it. An entry here is now a decision someone wrote down, not a promise to come back. Regenerate with `npm run check:ui-contract -- --update`.

reasons.raw-table: DataTable is the approved display-table contract. The rule exists to send feature code here; this is here.

reasons.raw-file-input: FileInput IS the approved picker contract, and its whole point is that the real `<input type="file">` is here rather than hand-built at a call site. Same shape of entry as DataTable's raw-table: the rule exists to send feature code here, and this is here.

reasons.hand-rolled-tablist: TabList IS the approved tab contract, so the one `role="tablist"` in the product that is not hand-rolled lives here. Same shape of entry as DataTable's raw-table: the rule exists to send feature code here.

reasons.raw-hex-colour: roadmap §5 — the hero's background wash is brand artwork: three decorative blobs blurred over 256–384px, aria-hidden, carrying no information, drawn in the mark's own colours. The named brand roles (--ds-color-brand-accent / -primary) cover everything on that panel that carries meaning; these three are translucent, and a Tailwind opacity modifier cannot be applied to a var() colour, so tokenising them would mean three single-use tint tokens for a blur.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — the campaign section rail. It is a `nav` of steps with `aria-current="step"` and a per-step completion indicator. `SectionNavigation` is the near miss and cannot express either: it hardcodes `aria-current="page"`, and it has no trailing slot for the complete/incomplete icon that is the whole point of this rail. Extending it for one consumer would be speculative; recorded as the section-rail-with-status gap instead. Tokenised, keyboard-reachable, shared focus ring.

roadmap §5 — the application-status filter chips are MULTI-select (a `status` array), and `SegmentedControl` is single-select by contract (`value` is a scalar). They are also 12px chips rather than 44px control-height cards, so adopting it would triple their height inside a filter panel. This is the filter-chip gap the catalog's Introduction already records, and this is its first concrete consumer.

roadmap §5 — two `role="menuitem"` entries in the card's overflow menu, plus one stat affordance inside the card body. `Button` renders `role="button"`, which would break the menu contract exactly as it would break the FMCSA combobox's `role="option"`; the stat affordance has no button chrome at all (no padding, no background, no border) and is a text-and-icon cell trigger. All three are tokenised and carry the shared focus ring.

reasons.raw-table: roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.
roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.

reasons.raw-palette-class: roadmap §5 — DeviceMockup is artwork, not interface. The bezel, side buttons and battery pips are moulded plastic, not a SafeHaul surface; mapping them onto --ds-color-surface-inverse-subtle would look identical today and would mean re-tuning the console surface silently restyles a picture of a phone. Declared once in the DEVICE constant at the top of the file. The screen itself takes --ds-color-surface.
reasons.sub-12px-type: roadmap §5 — the phone status-bar time is a decorative illustration of a real device, not interface text.
reasons.tailwind-radius: roadmap §5 — device artwork. The bezel and side-button radii describe a moulded plastic case, not a SafeHaul surface, and they are part of the same DEVICE palette exception as its colours.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — a selectable lead row on the inverse (console) surface, `aria-pressed` for its exclusion state. Same family as `CompanyChooserModal`'s selectable company row: it is correctly a `<button>` because it is a real activation, but forcing it into `Button` would make a virtualised list row look like an action bar. Uses only the on-inverse roles and the shared focus ring.

reasons.hand-styled-field: roadmap §5 — two borderless `<input type="date">` controls inside the leaderboard's date-range chip. Same gap as `ManageTeamModal`'s inline numeric editors: `Input` is a 44px bordered full-width control and would destroy the chip, and overriding it back would be worse. Both carry an `aria-label` and the shared focus ring. See the inline-editable-value gap in §5.

reasons.arbitrary-type-size: roadmap §5 — the 13px release-authorisation paragraph inside the generated 49 CFR §391.23 document. Same immutable export as this file's other entries: html2canvas rasterises it into a bare print window with no --ds-* properties, and VOEPreviewModal.export.test.jsx fails if the document acquires a token.
reasons.raw-palette-class: roadmap §5 — the generated 49 CFR §391.23 document is rasterised by html2canvas into a bare print window with no --ds-* custom properties, so a token would resolve to nothing. VOEPreviewModal.export.test.jsx enforces the boundary in both directions.
reasons.sub-12px-type: roadmap §5 — printed-form facsimile small print, not interface text.
reasons.tailwind-radius: roadmap §5 — the generated 49 CFR §391.23 document is rasterised by html2canvas into a bare print window with no --ds-* custom properties, so a tokenised radius would resolve to nothing on export. Enforced in both directions by VOEPreviewModal.export.test.jsx.
reasons.tailwind-shadow: roadmap §5 — the generated 49 CFR §391.23 document is rasterised by html2canvas into a bare print window with no --ds-* custom properties, so a tokenised shadow would resolve to nothing on export. Enforced in both directions by VOEPreviewModal.export.test.jsx.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — an FMCSA suggestion row is a three-line record summary (legal name, USDOT and location, then what FMCSA did or did not list), not a label. `SegmentedControl` takes a string `label`, so it cannot express this even though the semantics match; §5's claim that the primitive covers these rows was wrong and is corrected. This is the SelectableCard/Listbox gap. Tokenised, `aria-pressed`, shared focus ring.

reasons.raw-file-input: roadmap §5 — a PROGRAMMATIC picker: one hidden input opened by whichever per-employer "Upload Result" row action was activated. `FileInput` is a visible control by contract (a real input behind a real label), and there is no visible picker here to be — the affordance is a table row action. It carries an accessible name and the `hidden` attribute as well as the class, so it leaves the accessibility tree without depending on CSS.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — four dense-table affordances. Two 24px sort toggles in a column header and a 32px phone chip in a cell are both below the 36px `sm` step, which is the compact-icon-button gap the catalog's Introduction records; forcing the approved height would grow the header and the row. The third is the pipeline segment strip, whose 12px full-radius pills would become 44px cards under `SegmentedControl`, doubling the height of a filter strip that sits above a dense table. All four are tokenised, named per record where they act on one, and carry the shared focus ring.

reasons.raw-file-input: roadmap §5 — a PROGRAMMATIC picker. The visible affordance is one of two mutually exclusive intake choice cards ("Scan my CDL" beside "Fill Out Manually"), so it has to look like its sibling card rather than like a picker; `FileInput` is a visible control by contract. The input is `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order because the card is the control, and the card is a keyboard-reachable approved `Button`.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — an ARIA combobox option must carry role="option" inside the listbox, and `Button` renders role="button", which would break the combobox contract. No Combobox/Listbox primitive exists yet.

roadmap §5 — the SMTP setup-guide header. `Disclosure` has exactly one appearance, a rail-section header (12px, bold, uppercase, letter-spaced), because that is the shape its consumer needed; this is a card section heading at `heading-sm` with a description line under it, and `Disclosure` has no API for either. Giving the primitive a second visual variant for one consumer is speculative — recorded as the card-section-disclosure gap. The trigger itself is correct ARIA: `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on a button inside a heading, tokenised, shared focus ring.

reasons.raw-hex-colour: roadmap §5 — #1877F2 is Facebook's brand blue on the Facebook connection tile. A third-party mark is not a SafeHaul role and must not be re-tuned by a change to this product's palette, so it stays literal, the same way the SafeHaul mark's own colours are pinned rather than derived.

reasons.raw-table: roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — two ~14px accept/reject badges pinned to the corners of a suggestion box whose minimum size is 8px; `IconButton`'s min-height would overflow it. Both keep an accessible name, a focus-visible ring and --ds-* tones. Retiring them needs a compact icon-button size in the design system.

roadmap §5 — a mobile bottom app bar. Its items are equal-width stacked icon-over-label targets at 56px, which is the platform convention for a bottom bar and deliberately taller than the 44px control step; `Button` is an inline 44px control and cannot be either. No primitive covers a bottom app bar and one consumer does not justify writing one. Tokenised, each item named "Open <section>" so it does not collide with the heading inside the sheet it opens.

roadmap §5 — the field-palette tiles are colour-coded per field type, which is domain-to-visual mapping the feature owns and `Button` has no API for. Same exception family as the PEV FMCSA suggestion rows and the call-outcome grid: no approved SelectableCard/Listbox primitive yet.

roadmap §5 — a page thumbnail is a rendered PDF page image with a page number and field count, sized to the rail rather than to the control scale, and carries `aria-current="page"`. `Button` would put its own padding and background around a picture of a page. Same SelectableCard family as the FMCSA rows. Tokenised, uniquely named per page, shared focus ring.

reasons.hand-styled-field: roadmap §5 — the inline field-label editor sits inside the draggable field rectangle, whose minimum size is 8px. The approved `Input`'s control height would overflow the box it is labelling. Same exception family as this file's corner remove badge.
reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — the corner remove badge on a placed field box whose minimum size is 8px, because the geometry comes from the PDF's own coordinates. `IconButton`'s min-height would overflow the box it belongs to. Same constraint as this file's inline label editor. Keeps an accessible name, a focus-visible ring and `--ds-*` tones.

reasons.hand-styled-field: roadmap §5 — these inputs overlay author-placed PDF field boxes, whose geometry comes from the document's own coordinates and can be as small as 8px. The approved controls carry the shared 36/44/52px control height and inline padding, which would break alignment with the PDF. Same constraint already recorded for the signature button in this file.
reasons.off-scale-type: roadmap §5 — `text-base` is the 16px iOS no-zoom size. The design system solved this for `.ds-form-control` on 2026-08-25 (`--ds-font-size-control-mobile`), but these inputs are deliberately NOT `.ds-form-control`: they overlay author-placed PDF field boxes and cannot take the shared control styling, per the geometry exception above. The fix does not reach them, so they keep their own 16px.
reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — the signature affordance overlays an author-placed PDF field box, whose size comes from the document's coordinates and can be as small as 8px. Every approved control carries the shared 36/44/52px control height and inline padding, which would break alignment with the PDF underneath. Same constraint already recorded for this file's inputs.

reasons.raw-table: roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.
roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.
roadmap §5 — an operator console with six per-row actions and live progress. Uses the --ds-table-* roles. Per-row interactive rows are the case §5 approves a native table for.

roadmap §5 — a native table inside a virtualised scroll region. Uses the --ds-table-* roles. DataTable owns its own scroll container, so adopting it here would mean nesting two, which is the defect that produces a dead scrollbar gutter.
roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.

roadmap §5 — a native table with a per-row filter control and a per-row action, inside a dialog. Uses the --ds-table-* roles. Converting it to DataTable would need the editable-matrix decision that §6 still records as open.

roadmap §5 — three native tables with per-row actions. They use the --ds-table-* roles for header, divider and density, so they follow the approved table contract visually; DataTable is a display-table contract and does not cover per-row actions in three linked tables sharing one scroll region.

reasons.hand-styled-button: roadmap §5 — the sandbox-only Magic Fill control. It is a warning-toned action, and `Button` exposes primary/secondary/ghost/danger/link with no semantic status tone; the tone is load-bearing because the control fills a real application form with fabricated data and must not look like an ordinary step action. Already recorded in `design-system/README.md` as the sandbox Magic Fill exception. Tokenised, 44px activation height, shared focus ring.

reasons.hand-styled-anchor: A status-tinted phone chip that is also a tel: link. Fully tokenised with a screen-reader prefix ("Call now:"). Neither Link (underlined text) nor ButtonLink (button-shaped) is a tinted inline chip. See the tinted-chip-link gap in §5.

reasons.hand-styled-button: A selectable company row, not a button. It is correctly a <button> (it is a real activation), uses only --ds-* tokens and the shared focus ring. The rule cannot distinguish a tokenised selectable row from a hand-built button; forcing it into Button would make a list row look like an action bar.

reasons.hand-styled-field: Two inline numeric goal editors inside a labelled chip. Both are already tokenised, carry an aria-label and aria-invalid, and use the shared focus ring. `Input` is a 44px bordered full-width control and would destroy the compact inline chip; overriding it back would be worse than this. See the inline-editable-value gap in §5.

reasons.raw-table: roadmap §5 — approved native-table pattern for an editable matrix or per-row interactive rows. DataTable is a display-table contract. The table must still use the --ds-table-* roles.

reasons.raw-hex-colour: A print stylesheet, injected as a string into a bare print window that has no --ds-* custom properties — the same class of exception as the VOE export document. A token here would resolve to nothing and the page would print with no background.
